scope: Four spring 2025 packets substantively reviewed, with targeted later project comparisons. Other collected agendas and searchable minutes receive a separate relevance screen, not a full attachment audit.

findings.title: Potrero Phase II: funding changes and the recorded motion
findings.status: Combined motion recorded; minutes omit a carried result
findings.summary: The minutes combine the fourth CIP amendment, RCTC agreement amendment, three-party construction-funding agreement and TUMF amendment. The CIP proposal adds $5 million General Fund, $600,000 WRCOG TUMF and $2,402,257 in Tri Pointe TUMF credits, with $13.5 million Pass Zone TUMF intended for construction.
findings.limit: The minutes name a mover and seconder but omit the result and vote tally for this combined motion. Obtain the adopted CIP and executed agreements before treating the entire proposal as verified final authority. TUMF credit is not unrestricted cash revenue.

findings.title: Potrero agreement estimate and CIP totals are different measures
findings.summary: J.1 estimates the cooperative agreement at $75,819,000: $68,113,000 construction/construction management plus $7,706,000 PS&E/right-of-way. Its broader project table totals $79,306,257, pending the CIP amendment. I.1 shows a $79,252,046 component total and $71,904,000 current-budget caption; J.3 shows $78,952,046 with a $71,904,000 estimate caption.
findings.limit: The agreement estimate is not the whole CIP. Same-meeting captions and component totals are not internally uniform. Do not average them or pick a final project cost without the adopted CIP, RCTC agreement and reconciled ledger. These are historical estimates, not actual expenditure.

findings.title: Potrero TUMF: allocation versus reimbursement
findings.status: Terms proposed in the combined motion
findings.summary: J.3 proposes total Pass Zone TIP TUMF of $14.1 million. J.2 describes $13.5 million for construction, with WRCOG reimbursing RCTC directly after RCTC pays eligible costs. These figures have different scopes and are not two independent grants.
findings.limit: The combined minutes motion has no stated result. Executed agreements, eligible invoices and receipts remain to be checked. Project reimbursements do not establish restitution recovery or settlement payoff.

findings.title: PLUS amended for AB 98
findings.status: Adopted unanimously in a separate motion
findings.summary: Council adopted PLAN2024-0134, the AB 98 amendments to the Policy on Land Use and Sensitive Receptors. G.9 was considered separately from the initial consent motion covering G.1-G.7.
findings.limit: This confirms the timeline milestone and adds its complete packet route. It does not establish project-level compliance, enforcement results or a later policy version.

findings.title: Downtown parking suspension: first reading
findings.summary: Council approved the first reading extending the temporary parking suspension for existing non-residential downtown structures for up to 18 months.
findings.limit: This is not the second reading or an indefinitely continuing exemption. Check the final ordinance and effective/expiration dates before describing current parking requirements.

findings.title: Second Street Extension construction award
findings.summary: Council awarded MDB General Engineering $3,799,709 plus $379,970 contingency, for combined authority of $4,179,679. The report describes the roughly 2,525-foot extension to Pennsylvania Avenue and the previously awarded $1 million federal grant.
findings.limit: The grant is the same funding recorded in the October/December 2024 items, not another award to add again. Contract authority does not establish final spending or completion.

findings.title: Cherry Channel modeling amendment and accounting discrepancy
findings.summary: Council approved $9,600 of Chambers Group modeling work. The report states an original $164,566 environmental agreement and intended amended $174,166 contract, while its accounting table shows $174,566 encumbered.
findings.limit: Reconcile the $400 difference with the executed amendment and ledger. The discussion of approximately $1 million in possible mitigation credits is a forecast, not an approved purchase.

findings.title: Fairway Canyon emergency spending began at $500,000
findings.summary: The minutes record an emergency item added during the meeting, declaring a sewer-mainline emergency and authorizing expenditures up to $500,000 with continuing reports.
findings.limit: The late-added item is absent from the original packet inventory. The April increase to $1 million is cumulative, not $1 million plus the original $500,000. Spending requires ledger evidence.

findings.title: Special-event fee-waiver MOU was tabled
findings.summary: The proposed BCVRPD facility/park event fee-waiver MOU and resolution were tabled, rather than approved as recommended.
findings.limit: Do not treat the draft as executed or infer fees were waived. A later approval needs its own dated record.

findings.title: Sales-tax audit budget and purchase-order increase
findings.summary: The motion records a $960,115 sales-tax revenue amendment, $960,115.60 contractual-services amendment and $960,115.60 purchase-order increase for Hinderliter de Llamas & Associates.
findings.limit: Preserve the $0.60 difference and check the final adjustment. Approval is not payment evidence or unrestricted net revenue.

findings.title: Planning changes moved toward later hearings
findings.status: Directions and noticing, not completed adoptions
findings.summary: Council directed a home-occupation hearing process, requested short-term-rental information and directed notice of off-site-improvement and Planning Commission ordinance amendments.
findings.limit: These directions did not themselves adopt all ordinances. Track the April 1 first reading, April 15 second reading for Chapter 2.24 and separate off-site-improvement action.

findings.title: Federal project requests: Pennsylvania, Downtown and police campus
findings.summary: Attachment A requests $5 million for Pennsylvania grade separation, $2 million for Downtown revitalization and $2 million for a Public Safety and Cultural Complex master plan anchored by a new police station. It also lists $5 million for wildfire/infrastructure resilience and $2 million for a wastewater microgrid.
findings.limit: These are requests, not grants received or available construction funds. The 30-acre campus is a planning concept, not a final station footprint. Later awards must be checked separately.

findings.title: CFD refunding criteria and separate bond authorization
findings.status: Consensus on criteria; issuance approved unanimously
findings.summary: Council directed a 3% savings threshold and $200 savings in year two to screen refundings, with final transactions to return. Separately, it authorized CFD 2016-3 Series 2025 bonds up to $7.5 million and an acquisition-agreement amendment.
findings.limit: Screening criteria are not blanket refunding approval. An issuance ceiling is not the actual closing amount, cash receipt or expenditure.

findings.title: Cherry Festival: recorded $100,000 differs from the proposal
findings.summary: The minutes describe a $350,000 request but approve the already budgeted $100,000 through the balance of the entertainment invoice, with further contributions to return. Council also approved City hosting of the parade.
findings.limit: The packet recommended $135,000, which is not the recorded sponsorship amount. Check the later MOU and payments before calculating total event spending.

findings.title: Five-year financial audit services agreement
findings.summary: Council approved $337,125 over five years for Rogers, Anderson, Malody and Scott audit services, with annual engagement letters authorized.
findings.limit: This is the five-year total, not an annual cost. Completed audits, engagement letters and payments need separate records.

findings.title: Wastewater bids rejected; emergency reporting continued
findings.status: Rebid approved unanimously; follow-up directed by consensus
findings.summary: Council rejected WW24-01 Bid Package 1 bids and authorized revised documents and re-advertisement. The emergency item separately required another response, expenditure and timeline report.
findings.limit: Rejecting bids is not an award or completion. Continued emergency reporting does not itself create another spending authorization.

findings.title: Police specialized-equipment inventory received
findings.summary: Council received the annual specialized-equipment inventory and fiscal-impact report.
findings.limit: Receiving an inventory does not authorize new purchases or complete the separate station project. Use the attachment for inventory and cost details.

findings.title: Fairway Canyon emergency ceiling increased to $1 million
findings.summary: Council increased City Manager authority by $500,000 to a cumulative $1,000,000 and extended the emergency declaration, with another follow-up required.
findings.limit: The ceiling includes the March $500,000. It does not prove $1 million was spent or repairs completed.

findings.title: Mesa Lift Station water-service agreement and bonds
findings.summary: Council authorized the BCVWD service agreement and performance/payment bonds of $103,162.50 for the Mesa Lift Station Upgrade Project.
findings.limit: Bond face value is security, not necessarily cash expenditure to add to construction costs. Check the agreement, premiums and payments.

findings.title: Beaumont Nights: season estimate and fee-process direction
findings.summary: Staff estimates $305,106 in non-personnel operating expenses and $202,995 personnel for the 2025 season, totaling $508,101. Council directed notice of a vendor fee/deposit hearing and allowed alcohol sales subject to ABC licensing.
findings.limit: This is a season estimate spanning fiscal-year budgets, not actual expenditure or a three-year total. Notice of a fee hearing is not fee adoption. Check invoices, payroll allocation and later decisions.

findings.title: Pennsylvania grants: pending requests versus awards
findings.status: Quarterly report received through unanimous consent
findings.summary: The Q3 summary lists $25 million applied for January 30 and $5 million applied for March 27. The scanned pending table also lists a $50.4 million TCEP request. A $22.6 million STBG request appears in the future-quarter outlook.
findings.limit: These are requests in the March 31 snapshot, not funds to sum. The summary calls the January request RAISE while detail calls it BUILD; identify the application rather than counting both names. Later 2026 funding/withdrawal records supersede these statuses.
documentTitles: Attachment C - Pending Grant Applications Detail

findings.title: Stewart Park ORLP: historical $3.1 million listing
findings.summary: The scanned Active Grants Detail lists a $3.1 million Outdoor Recreation Legacy Program grant for Stewart Park, dated September 25, 2024, with December 31, 2027 end date.
findings.limit: This is a Q3 FY2024-25 register snapshot, not cash received or a current balance. Keep it distinct from the later $2.5 million preserved-funding figure; do not add the two as independent grants.

findings.title: SB 125 project labels need reconciliation
findings.summary: Active Grants Detail labels a $5 million SB 125/TIRCP award as Potrero, dated July 23, 2024. The October 15, 2024 CIP report attributes a $5 million SB 125 increase to Pennsylvania grade separation.
findings.limit: This is a project-label discrepancy, not evidence of two awards. Obtain the allocation resolution, award agreement and project ledger before reassigning funds or increasing confirmed funding.

relatedSources.title: October 15, 2024 CIP report: Pennsylvania SB 125 allocation (packet page 55)

findings.title: Potrero landscaping creates an operating obligation
findings.summary: Council approved the Caltrans maintenance agreement. Staff describes three years of plant establishment plus 17 years of maintenance, for 20 years, with costs from Community Services operations.
findings.limit: This is not completion or a quantified maintenance appropriation. Caltrans takeover after 20 years requires coordination, not automatic termination. Obtain execution, mapped areas and costs.

findings.title: CRC overflow parking: Council chose Option 1 conditionally
findings.summary: Council authorized Option 1 if within budget, rather than the recommended Option 3 study. Staff identifies $224,400 allocated to P-23 and says Option 1 lights the pedestrian path without adequately lighting the full lot.
findings.limit: Budget, SCE approvals and completion remain separate checks. This is Community Recreation Center parking, not Stewart Park construction.

findings.title: Ladder truck direction uses an existing purchase request
findings.summary: Council directed County Fire to acquire an identified truck to fulfill the existing request. Staff cites the earlier $2,205,646.81 purchase order and says no new funding is requested.
findings.limit: Do not count the earlier purchase order as a new April appropriation or infer delivery, staffing or deployment.

findings.title: Planning follow-through: relief and continued hearings
findings.summary: Council unanimously approved the off-site-improvement suspension motion and Chapter 2.24 second reading. Noble Creek Vistas repeal continued to June 3; home occupations continued to May 6.
findings.limit: Continuances do not adopt a repeal or home-occupation amendment. This is not a PLUS amendment. Check final instruments and later decisions for current requirements.

findings.title: Procurement and grant reports are not new awards
findings.status: Consent reports received; CUCCAC acknowledgment result unstated
findings.summary: Council received purchase/contract and grant reports. The grant summary distinguishes $63,890,896.29 listed active grants, $91,900,831.70 pending applications and $108,000 awarded in the period. The CUCCAC item records a motion to acknowledge its February 14 letter.
findings.limit: Different populations must not be added as available cash. The CUCCAC minutes omit the result; acknowledgment alone does not resolve its issues. Check awards, procurement records and corrective actions.

findings.title: Classification and compensation study ceiling
findings.summary: Council awarded Evergreen Solutions $152,000 for one year plus $30,400 contingency, totaling $182,400 authority.
findings.limit: The total already includes contingency. The award does not establish completed deliverables, salary changes or actual spending.

findings.title: Stewart Park: November proposal refreshes schedule evidence
findings.summary: The November 17 report says Phase II design is complete and seeks plans/specifications approval and bid solicitation. It anticipates 45 days of advertising and January 2027 bids. It reports Phase I progress and a March 2027 contractual completion schedule, with weather-delay risk.
findings.limit: This upcoming-meeting report is not bid authorization, an issued notice, award or confirmed completion. It is more specific than the October forecast. Verify the actual disposition and issued bid notice.
documentTitles: Staff Report - Stewart Park Phase 2 Plans and Specifications

findings.title: October 20 draft minutes are collected; approval pending
findings.summary: The packet includes draft October 20 minutes. The station motion records $219,752 Phase I services plus $21,975 contingency, totaling $241,727, with later phases subject to funding and Council authorization. The Downtown draft records direction to proceed and amend the STB agreement.
findings.limit: These drafts do not establish approved minutes as of November 13 or corrected executed contracts. The $18,000 option exclusion and corrected Downtown $68,850 design total remain tied to transcript discussion; do not attribute those corrections to a draft clause that does not state them.

findings.title: Police network and Axon proposals include separate costs and scope checks
findings.status: Upcoming recommendations; no approval or payment claimed
findings.summary: Staff proposes $125,636.94 for the CDCE police-vehicle network upgrade and a separate $130,314.94 Axon addition. The existing packet review identifies bundled AI Assistant/Draft One services of $40,512 in the Axon quote, a 50-month quote term and June 2028 payment date versus the staff report's four-year description and July 2028 payment timing.
findings.limit: These are separate proposed agreements, not police-station construction or actual expenditure. Clarify the authorized service scope and controlling payment schedule; the quote total agreeing with the report does not resolve the term and scope differences. No November 17 outcome is recorded here.
documentTitles: Staff Report - Police Vehicles Network Device Upgrade
Staff Report - Approve the Purchase of Additional Body-Worn Cameras and Licenses

findings.title: November budget proposal: adjustment total and description conflict
findings.status: Upcoming recommendation; financial results attributed to staff
findings.summary: Staff reports $15.2 million General Fund first-quarter spending, about 19.3% of the $78.5 million budget. Its recommended adjustment table totals $1,643,493. The collected packet review notes that a $53,000 Planning adjustment is labeled Weed Abatement in the summary but Golden Triangle annexation professional services on the adjustment form.
findings.limit: Do not label the entire adjustment as new City spending: distinguish appropriations, transfers and coding corrections. Finance needs to reconcile the $53,000 description. The published proposal does not establish Council approval, payment or a revised adopted budget.
documentTitles: Staff Report - 1st Quarter FY27 Budget vs. Actuals

findings.title: Vactor truck proposal stays separate from the wastewater project budget
findings.status: Upcoming purchase request; no outcome claimed
findings.summary: Staff requests $741,255.35 for a Vactor sewer-cleaning truck through Haaker Equipment Company and Sourcewell. The report identifies an $826,699 budget for WW27-01 from Wastewater Repair and Replace funds.
findings.limit: The $85,443.65 difference is arithmetic against the project budget, not proof of uncommitted funds or realized savings. A purchase request is not an executed order, delivery or actual expenditure.
